title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding minimization (v29)
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve throughput and unit-cost for production traffic by reducing padding overhead and improving scheduling efficiency in the continuous-batching runtime. Prior approaches used coarse fixed buckets which led to excess padding for long-tail sequences and suboptimal kernel selection. This PR introduces an adaptive seqlen bucketing heuristic that minimizes padding while keeping scheduling and kernel selection stable under high concurrency.

Summary of changes: Updated the batching scheduler to maintain dynamic buckets keyed by percentiles of active sequence-length distribution. Each bucket records a moving-window histogram and uses a cost model to decide when to merge/split buckets to balance padding waste vs scheduling overhead. Added a padding-trimming pass that opportunistically packs shorter sequences into spare slots within a batch when KV cache and attention state allow. Tied kernel selection to bucket metadata so runtime picks the fastest kernel configuration for the expected max-seqlen in the bucket. Tuned the heuristics to avoid thrashing when the workload has bursty long sequences.

Key benefits: Reduced average padding tokens by ~32% on mixed chat workloads and improved overall throughput by 12% on A100 80GB clusters; p95 latency increased by <2% in stress scenarios. Improvements are most pronounced for workloads with multimodal length distributions (chat + embeddings).

Benchmarks: Microbench harness (bench/continuous_batching) with production-like trace replay (100k requests): baseline vs this branch on 8xA100: tokens/sec +12%, token-cost-per-100k -9%. Long-tail test (10% sequences >2k tokens): padding reduction 41%, throughput +18%.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated. Start with canary on Dedicated stubs (10% traffic) for 48h, monitor token-cost, p90/p95 latency, and kernel error rates. If stable, expand to 50% then 100% over one week. Canary config is enabled via runtime flag runtime.batch.seqlen_adaptive=true.

Operational notes: Added new metrics runtime.batch.bucket_count, runtime.batch.avg_padding_tokens, runtime.batch.bucket_split_rate; dashboards and alerts are included in observability-pack change. KV cache semantics: when trimming padding we ensure KV cache alignment constraints are preserved; trimming is disabled for models with dynamic kv offset kernels until kernel is validated.

Files and scope: Small localized runtime changes (scheduler, batch packing, kernel selection hook), a new cost model module, unit tests, and e2e microbench harness updates. No API changes.

Risk and mitigations: The most significant risk is increased scheduling jitter from aggressive bucket churn; mitigations include hysteresis windows, minimum bucket lifetime, and conservative default cost thresholds. Additional safety toggles added to disable adaptive splitting at runtime.

Related: builds on prior iterations in this repo (see pr-115678, pr-111333, pr-104679) and ties into ENG-1452 for kernel selection telemetry.

Change log (high level): - scheduler: introduce AdaptiveSeqlenBucketer with percentile histogram - packing: padding-trimming pass with KV-cache checks - kernels: bucket-driven kernel_hint metadata and selection API - metrics: new batch/padding telemetry - tests: unit tests + e2e benchmarks
